lines: In these generated files gitleaks matches only rules that take any string of high entropy, which hashes and minified names are as well, or the curl lines a page of built documentation copies from its source, so the matches are not reported as secrets:
js/larpingapp-main.js.map, a source map: 24 matches in 4 commits (sourcegraph-access-token).
js/larpingapp-settings.js.map, a source map: 18 matches in 3 commits (sourcegraph-access-token).
assets/js/9985b2a0.2b2a219f.js, a page of built documentation: 2 matches in 1 commit (curl-auth-user).
assets/js/9985b2a0.d8c46a74.js, a page of built documentation: 2 matches in 1 commit (curl-auth-user).
A key a build takes from the environment ends up in such a file too: where one of them has no reason to carry a key, look at it.
In these files gitleaks matches values that stand for a credential, such as admin:admin or <password>, so the matches are not reported as secrets:
The values are the list secrets-placeholders.json of ncmake.

These files are test data, the report of a test run or example code, whose keys and tokens are made up or serve a test, so the matches are not reported as secrets. Those of a private key or a GitHub token are:
newman/newman-run-report-2026-03-10-12-20-22-632-0.json, the report of a test run: 310 matches in 1 commit (jwt).
A token a test run used against a real server stays valid until it is revoked: where one of these files holds one, revoke it.
